stem: Amberfield Robotics sets an optional resource argument to `null` in their configuration. What is the practical effect?

choices.text: Terraform stores an empty string in place of the argument's real value
Terraform stores the number zero in place of the argument's real value, treating `null` as equivalent to a numeric zero
Terraform treats `null` as an error and refuses to plan the configuration
Terraform treats the argument as omitted, falling back to its default or an error

rationale: Setting an argument to null is Terraform's way of expressing that the argument was not set at all -- its default kicks in, or Terraform errors if the argument is mandatory and has no default. null is not the same value as an empty string or a numeric zero; both of those are real, present values, while null represents the absence of one. null is also a valid, typeless literal in the language, not an error.
